candidates.description: Dave's clocks forgive each honest response only one response budget G: Clock.pauseAfterResponseAt stores allowance - max(elapsed - G, 0) and nothing ever gives the excess back (a child return refills only T + 2G, the join deducts lateness with no discount). The released deployment policy fixes G = 5 minutes on every chain, i.e. 25 blocks on Ethereum/Sepolia, and the root allowance A = C + 2G + (T + 2G) with C = 1 week on mainnets (A = 51,100 blocks) and C = 8 hours on testnets (A = 3,100 blocks). The threat model's honest operator 'acts only on history that its policy treats as final, such as finalized blocks', and 'acting on history before it is final, and recovering when that history is replaced, is outside this model'. On Ethereum a block becomes final 65 to 96 blocks after it is produced, so such an operator cannot answer a bisection turn in fewer than about 66 blocks: every one of its responses is charged at least 41 blocks (57 at the mean lag of 80), although it reacts as fast as its chain view allows. Dave's own design note says the budget only works because 'a joined match's responses read latest and do not wait for [finality]', i.e. the released G is sized for an operator that acts on non-final history, which this threat model excludes. The number of charged responses is chosen by the adversary: a root match costs the honest side 27 responses (height 54), a leaf match 19 plus the proof, and Dave's asynchronous pairing lets Sybil claims meet the honest claim one after another (pairCommitment pairs each joiner or re-entering survivor with the dangling honest commitment; Dave's docs/dispute-game.md:354-368 and docs/prt-delay-bound.md 'Post-closure staggered release' give about 75 sequential root matches at delta = G within one allowance after closure, two bonds each). Once the honest clock is at or below one response latency, advanceMatch reverts with CannotAdvanceTimedOutClock, the Sybil claims winMatchByTimeout, and a fabricated root claim can finish the root and be staged. No policy satisfies both sides: a final-only operator overruns G on every response, and the recipe's default (dispute policy depth 4, 'a confirmation depth is a policy, not finality') acts on history the model does not cover.
candidates.trigger: Any party that can post claims (bonds only). It posts a Sybil root claim that meets the honest claim (join while the honest claim is dangling, e.g. one block before closure with a 1-block clock and same-block replies, or a Sybil pair whose timeout re-pairs the survivor with the dangling honest commitment), answers its own turns at once, and abandons on its last turn. Repeat with further Sybils; inside a forced child tournament each leaf Sybil costs the honest claim 20 more charged actions and is removed at once by the honest proof, so leaf Sybils can be chained back to back. No censorship, no reorg and no invalid proof is needed.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on every Ethereum-timed deployment made with the released Deployment.s.sol whenever the honest operator observes dispute events at 'finalized' (the only observation the threat model covers, and the PRT player's own default for inputs and seals). Arithmetic with the released constants (clocksim.py re-implements Clock.pauseAfterResponseAt and ClockBudgets): Sepolia-class testnets (C = 8 h): the honest clock expires in the 2nd forced root match at a finality lag of 80 or 96 blocks (after 53 or 41 honest responses) and in the 3rd at the best-case lag of 65; Ethereum mainnet (C = 1 week): in the 27th, 34th or 47th forced root match at lags 96, 80, 65. On the testnet constants two matches fit inside Dave's own documented regime (one match before closure, one staggered release after it). On mainnet one allowance of staggered releases removes about 70% of the clock (23 matches x 27 x 56 blocks at lag 80), and the rest needs either leaf Sybils inside a forced child (about 820 blocks per leaf match, chained) or releases later than one allowance after closure (Sybil pairs parked in sealed inner matches); I derived both by reading the rules and did not replay them on chain. With a dispute policy of depth 4 (delta about 5-6 blocks) nothing is charged.

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded. The exclusion 'Defects that need the deployment to violate one of A1 to A8, unless ... an implementation of the referee model is what violates it (section 3)' keeps it in: the released Dave constants are the referee model's own. The trigger does not need a reorganization or an operator acting early; it needs the operator the model defines ('The honest operator acts only on history that its policy treats as final, such as finalized blocks').
rating_steps.2_role: Dave is 'Referee model, as the deployed referee. Audit the released constants'. Section 3: 'A defect that only changes how long a claim may take to respond ... is rated as support.' The defect is the size of the response budget, so the support rating applies under the preferred reading.
rating_steps.3_high_medium: Medium: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. In the deployed-referee role it is Critical (step 4), so Medium.
rating_steps.4_critical: Alternative reading (the one preferred for R1-A7-1): the clocks are part of what the deployed referee decides, and A7 is violated on the honest operator's path: 'The dispute constants and clocks leave room for the honest claim to play the ... matches that a tournament forces on it ... No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock.' and R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks.' The honest claim is eliminated, so 'a dishonest claim can win' (section 1, completeness failure). Then Critical.
rating_steps.5_low: Low if the operator's dispute observation policy is read as free ('history that its policy treats as final' with a 4-block policy): then the released G covers the operator and only a documentation gap remains (the manual and the threat model do not say that Dave's budget requires acting on non-final history). Facts that decide: whether a production validator may respond from 'latest', and whether section 3's support clause covers Dave's clock sizing.

candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred: clock sizing of the referee model, support rating of a Critical A7 violation); Critical if Dave's clock constants are rated as the deployed referee's own decision, as R1-A7-1 preferred; Low if a shallow dispute policy counts as final
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness failure of section 1: 'The honest operator ... cannot respond in time. If the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim can win.' An honest operator that follows the model's chain-trust rule loses its root clock to response charges alone, the Sybil wins by timeout, and its fabricated final state (with any outputs root) can be staged and accepted. On testnet constants this costs two or three bonds; on mainnet tens of bonds.

candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh on the local chain with the released Dave build: deploy CanonicalTournamentParametersProvider with the released Sepolia arguments (12000, 28800, 300) and a factory; instantiate a root; join the honest commitment 66 blocks after the start and a synthetic Sybil commitment (trees that differ at a chosen leaf, as Dave's own tests build them); mine 65 blocks before each honest advanceMatch and let the Sybil answer in the next block; when the Sybil abandons, claim the timeout and release the next Sybil. Assert the property A7 requires for an operator that answers every turn within one finality delay: commitmentStanding(honest).clockAllowance never decreases (or: the honest advanceMatch never reverts with CannotAdvanceTimedOutClock). On the released constants the allowance drops by 41 per response and the second or third match reverts, so the test exits 1; it exits 0 once the response budget covers the finality delay the operator must wait for (or the model states that responses may be sent from non-final history).

candidates.title: Dave's asynchronous pairing lets Sybils force a number of matches on the honest claim that is linear in the number of claims, where the manual and A7 assume a logarithmic number
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 prt/contracts Tournament.pairCommitment / joinTournament / winMatchByTimeout (pairing and re-pairing), against doc/README.md 'Permissionless refereed tournament' and THREAT_MODEL A7 / section 7
candidates.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee; the manual side is the normative referee model
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/prt/contracts/src/tournament/Tournament.sol:1182-1224 (pairCommitment), :214-243 (joinTournament), :298-367 (winMatchByTimeout re-pairs the survivor in the same call); bugs/harness/work/dave/released/docs/dispute-game.md:354-368 and docs/prt-delay-bound.md:240-256 (Dave's own statement of the linear regime); doc/README.md:10401-10403, :10434 ('About log2 N' rounds), :11310-11313 (listed simplification about pairing order); THREAT_MODEL.md A7 and section 7
candidates.description: In Dave a tournament has one dangling slot, and every commitment that joins or wins is paired with whatever is dangling. A correct commitment that wins a match becomes dangling again, so each Sybil that the adversary releases next (a fresh join before closure, or after closure the survivor of a Sybil pair whose timeout the adversary triggers at a chosen block) meets the honest commitment directly. The honest claim therefore plays one full match per released Sybil, not ceil(log2 N). Dave's documentation states it: 'A skewed arrival schedule can force a correct survivor through a number of matches linear in the claims', about 988 sequential root matches at one-block responses and 75 at delta = G within one allowance after closure, at two bonds per match. The manual describes PRT as settling 'in a number of rounds logarithmic in N, and Dave builds on it' and tabulates 'About log2 N'; A7 sizes clocks for 'the logarithmic number of matches that a tournament forces on it', section 7 lets the adversary 'force the honest claim through a logarithmic number of matches', and R12 asks A7 to cover the cost of reaching the disputed position 'a bounded number of times for every match ... that the tournaments force on the honest claim'. The manual's list of simplifications mentions the pairing order but not that it changes the number of matches the honest claim must play. In Dave the clock holds for any number of matches only because every action is discounted separately; any per-match honest cost above G or T (the confirmed R1-A7-1, R1-A7-3, R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-1, R3-VARGROWTH-1, R3-VARSCHED-1/2, or the finality delay of the first candidate) is therefore multiplied by a number the adversary chooses, not by log2 N.
candidates.trigger: An adversary that posts k Sybil root claims (bonds only) and times their joins or the timeouts of Sybil-versus-Sybil matches so that one Sybil at a time is paired with the dangling honest commitment.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on the released contracts by construction (pairCommitment has no bracket); Dave's property tests StaggeredReleaseWork.t.sol and DelayPerRootBond.t.sol, cited by its docs, exercise it. I did not run them.

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded as such. The manual lists 'Each claim that joins meets the one waiting ... The model gathers a tournament's claims first and runs the bracket in rounds' as a simplification, and listed simplifications 'are not normative'; triage may read the linear count as part of that simplification.
rating_steps.2_role: Dave: referee model as the deployed referee. The disagreement is not in what the referee verifies or which claim a timeout decides, but in how many matches it forces, which bears on response time only: 'A defect that only changes how long a claim may take to respond ... is rated as support.'
rating_steps.3_high_medium: No listed High or Medium case fits by itself: with every per-action cost inside G and T the honest clock is never charged, so the count alone eliminates nothing.
rating_steps.4_critical: No rule is violated by the count alone. R12 allows the honest operator's work to grow 'with the inputs, yields, and matches of the epochs still open'. A7's wording ('the logarithmic number of matches') describes the manual's bracket, not Dave.
rating_steps.5_low: Low: a real mismatch between the deployed referee and the manual's and threat model's premise, with no rule violated on its own. It is reported because it is the multiplier of every per-match latency finding, and as a gap in the threat model (A7 and section 7 assume a bound that the pinned referee does not give).

candidates.claimed_severity: Low (gap between A7/section 7/the manual's 'About log2 N' and the pinned Dave contracts); it raises the impact of every confirmed per-match latency issue from 'times log2 N' to 'times the number of Sybil bonds'
candidates.threat_to_goal: Not a break by itself. It removes the margin the goal's sizing argument relies on: the honest claim's total uncompensated latency is (per-match excess) x (matches), and the second factor is adversary-chosen and linear, so a small per-match excess that A7 would absorb over log2 N matches becomes an elimination (completeness failure) over tens or hundreds of matches.
candidates.evidence: Read Tournament.sol pairing and Dave's docs/dispute-game.md and docs/prt-delay-bound.md (living documents, not review records). No experiment.
candidates.test_idea: A chain test on the released Dave build that joins N synthetic Sybil commitments with the schedule of Dave's StaggeredReleaseWork property test and counts MatchCreated events that involve the honest commitment; assert count <= ceil(log2(N + 1)). It fails (count grows as N/2). Alternatively a documentation check: the manual's list of simplifications must state that Dave's pairing can force a linear number of matches on a claim.

not_covered: No on-chain run: nothing was executed on the local chain harness or with forge. The two candidates rest on reading the released sources and on clocksim.py, a re-implementation of ClockBudgets and Clock.pauseAfterResponseAt; the mainnet schedule past one allowance after closure (parked Sybil pairs, chained leaf Sybils in a forced child) was derived by reading and not replayed.

Checked by reading, no candidate (released Dave Tournament/Clock/MatchClocks/Time/Match/factory/DaveConsensus): join deduction and closure; pairing and the dangling clock start; response discount; timeout classification in bisection and in the leaf race (earlier-deadline rule, equal deadlines, deferred charge, pauseWinnerAt positivity); sealed inner matches cannot be deleted except through their recorded child; child allowance max(r1, r2); child-return allowance min(carried + T + 2G, envelope) and its conservation for an operator inside G and T + G; winner expiry [resultAt, resultAt + clock) and that resultAt is never retroactive; no stuck match or child state; adversary acting for the honest side (early joins of the honest commitment at either level, playing its moves, sealing in the pairing block) charges the honest clock at most what its own join lateness would; ROOT_FAILED and root closure; asserts on progress paths. Under Dave's own latency bounds (every action within G, child join within T + G) I found no rule that charges or eliminates the honest claim.

Bond and refund economics: whether front-run or expired honest transactions (for example a winLeafMatch that lands after the opponent's leaf clock expired and pays the EIP-7623 calldata floor without refund) can drain the honest signer below a join bond; refund conservation; winner payment. Only the timing side of bonds was read (a bond is needed for each child join, one at a time).

Gas limit of the PRT journal (2 x eth_estimateGas) against the pairing branch an adversary can switch on between estimate and inclusion: estimated from storage writes at about 1.6-1.8x for joinTournament and winMatchByTimeout, not measured.

Non-Ethereum registrations of the released Deployment.s.sol (OP Stack 2 s blocks, Arbitrum's parent-chain block number): block-number clock semantics, finality and sequencer delays were not analysed beyond noting that OP Stack finality (L1 finality) also exceeds G = 150 L2 blocks.

The referee model in doc/recipes (prt.lua, game-transport.lua): clocks, windows and join deadlines were re-read against the manual (wait_at_most excludes the deadline block, claim allowances, timeout-win and elimination windows, uarch tournament admission); no new derivation defect found. Not fuzzed, not run with custom late or racing adversaries.

PRT bridge and journal (support): job windows, leaf-race handover, inner-tournament windows, tick ordering and submit were re-read against Dave; no new candidate beyond the confirmed R1-A8-4, R3-VARSCHED-1/2 and the pending R6-DYNBRIDGE-1..3. Not run against adversaries that perform the honest side's moves or that join one block before closure.

Cost of the honest player's per-match actions under the released geometry (p = 18): child build against T, root and uarch bundle opening and leaf proof against G with this emulator were not measured (R1-A7-1 territory); restart cost against the clocks was not measured.
Tournaments with more than two levels, the Rust validator node, the Cartesi Rollups Node, ZK, and Dave's docs/reviews (deliberately not read).
